statement: Let W=sum_(i,j)d_ij[|ij>]-kappa[omega], omega=sum_i|ii>, with arbitrary nonnegative real d_ij and kappa>0. For pair e={i,j} write q_e=sqrt(d_ij*d_ji). For each of the three perfect matchings M={e,f}, let m_M=1 if max(q_e,q_f)=0, and otherwise m_M=min(1,kappa/max(q_e,q_f)). If sum_M m_M>=1, every 2-block-positive W is decomposable, with NO restriction on or equality between the four d_ii. Independently, if the graph of pairs q_e<kappa is disconnected, every 2-block-positive W is decomposable. Consequently an indecomposable 2-block-positive member, if one exists, must have the q_e<kappa edges forming exactly a spanning star and must satisfy sum_(e in the complementary high triangle) kappa/q_e<1. This necessary obstruction is not a construction or a general nonexistence result.
matching_test: For arbitrary real z_i>=0 and a matching M={ij,kl}, take a direct sum of two rank-one 2x2 coefficient blocks having diagonal entries (z_i,z_j) and (z_k,z_l), with offdiagonal products z_i*z_j and z_k*z_l. Optimizing their absolute values yields the necessary all-variable inequality f_M(z)=sum_i d_ii*z_i^2-kappa*(sum_i z_i)^2+2(q_ij*z_i*z_j+q_kl*z_k*z_l)>=0. Zero coefficients and zero z_i are included by limits. This is a test on rank<=2 vectors, not a claim that these tests alone characterize 2-block positivity.
matching_decomposition: Assume S=sum_M m_M>=1 and choose p_M=m_M/S. Then 0<=p_M<=1, sum p_M=1, and p_M*q_e<=kappa for each e in M. For e={i,j} in its unique perfect matching M(e), let B_e=p_M(e)*[[d_ij,-q_e],[-q_e,d_ji]] on span{|ij>,|ji>}. Each B_e is PSD and B=sum_e B_e is PSD. The off-diagonal-basis entries of A=W-B^Gamma are (1-p_M(e))*d_ij>=0. Its correlated block H has H_ii=d_ii-kappa and H_ij=p_M(e)*q_e-kappa<=0. For every z>=0, z^T H z=sum_M p_M*f_M(z)>=0. A real symmetric matrix with nonpositive offdiagonal entries that is nonnegative on the nonnegative orthant is PSD: for every real x, x^T H x>=|x|^T H|x|>=0; complex vectors follow by splitting real and imaginary parts. Thus A>=0 and W=A+B^Gamma.
disconnected_low_graph: Let G have vertices 0,1,2,3 and edges q_e<kappa. If G is disconnected, all its components C have size at most 3. For every cross-component pair e={i,j}, q_e>=kappa; let B_e=(kappa/q_e)*[[d_ij,-q_e],[-q_e,d_ji]], PSD. Its partial transpose cancels exactly the -kappa |ii><jj| terms, leaving nonnegative diagonal cross-pair remainders. For each component C, the remaining principal restriction W_C=sum_(i,j in C)d_ij[|ij>]-kappa[sum_(i in C)|ii>] is 2-block positive. It is PSD for |C|<=2 and decomposable for |C|=3 by Yang-Leung-Tang, https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.03534. Lift each component decomposition and add the cross-pair remainder and B^Gamma. This covers arbitrary unequal diagonal coefficients.
only_remaining_topology: If S<1, every perfect matching has an edge q_e>kappa; otherwise that matching alone would have m_M=1. If G is also connected, it has at least three edges, while its complement has at most three. The complement therefore has exactly one strict-high edge in each perfect matching, and G is a three-edge spanning tree. Three edges containing one from each perfect matching are either a star or a triangle. The complement of a high star is a disconnected low triangle; since G is connected, the high graph must be a triangle and G its complementary spanning star. The matching maxima are then the three high-triangle q values, so S=sum_high kappa/q_e<1.
unequal_diagonal_nontrivial_example: Add (1/2)[|00>] to the predecessor's rigorously 2-block-positive W0=(1/2)I+3 sum_i[|ii>]-[omega]. The new diagonal coefficients are d_00=4 and d_11=d_22=d_33=7/2, with every offdiagonal d_ij=1/2. It remains 2-block positive, is not PSD since <omega|W|omega>=-3/2, and is not coPSD since <01+10|W^Gamma|01+10>=-1. Here all m_M=1 so the matching theorem applies even though the low graph is connected. The predecessor's exact example checker is frontier-20261028-matching-witness-check.py SHA256 6b7694d3c254f38c03efadaa70e6bef8ff97e78445487232974e6b32f85ef6d2; the added diagonal and changed test value are elementary exact arithmetic.
arbitrary_correlated_negative_ket: For psi=sum_i c_i|ii> with all c_i nonzero, an invertible diagonal Bob congruence sends psi to omega and transforms q_ij to sqrt(d_ij*d_ji)/|c_i*c_j| while allowing completely arbitrary transformed diagonal d_ii/|c_i|^2. Thus both criteria and the star-only necessary condition apply to all such diagonal-minus-[psi] witnesses. If psi has Schmidt rank at most 3, the full family is already decomposable by the 3x3 argument in frontier-20261028-weighted-correlated-witness-nogo-v1.json SHA256 1d7b840497758d6a5933beb122d10512a469d515adde32a7d7642c5f2050fb7d.
limits: The star condition is necessary only, not sufficient for a 2-block-positive indecomposable witness; no such witness or PPT/SN3 state has been constructed. The matching proof is all-variable elementary WRITTEN reasoning, with the 3x3 theorem explicitly imported for the disconnected case. No external/formal review or novelty claim.
